identity_marker: dark graphite Herman Miller Aeron chair with a woven pellicle mesh back and a removable horizontal lumbar support pad
continuity_anchors: in a brightly lit modern office space with white walls and soft natural daylight
video_goal: Demonstrate how to adjust the height and depth of the lumbar support pad on a Herman Miller Aeron chair.
single_prompt: A medium shot captures a person standing behind an empty dark graphite Herman Miller Aeron chair with a woven pellicle mesh back and a removable horizontal lumbar support pad in a brightly lit modern office space with white walls and soft natural daylight. The camera focuses closely on the horizontal lumbar support pad resting on the vertical tracks directly behind the mesh. From an over-the-shoulder view, the person's hands reach out and firmly grasp both outer edges of the lumbar support pad. The hands slide the lumbar pad smoothly upward along the vertical tracks to the highest position. Next, the hands slide the lumbar pad downward to the lowest position on the tracks. In an extreme close-up, the fingers grip the textured rubber edge of the pad, preparing to remove it for depth adjustment. The hands pull the lumbar pad firmly backward, snapping it completely off the vertical tracks. From a first-person view, the hands rotate the removed lumbar pad 180 degrees to reveal the thicker, more pronounced side of the pad. The hands align the grooves on the thicker side of the pad with the vertical tracks on the chair frame. The hands push forward, snapping the lumbar pad securely back onto the tracks. The person walks around to the front of the chair and sits down on the seat pan. From a side profile view, the person leans back into the pellicle mesh, pressing their lower back against the newly adjusted lumbar pad.
